html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; URL: uniform resource locator

  • The anatomy of a Messages API request and response
  • Why the API is stateless and how multi-turn conversations work
  • Streaming: the event sequence and how to assemble the result
  • Multi-format input: images, PDFs and the Files API, with their limits
  • The usage fields and the stop_reason values

2A Request and Its Response

Running case

Tidewater's First Call

  • An adjuster asks: "Summarize claim 4471 and list any missing documents."
  • The developer sends the policy text and the claim notes to Claude and wants the answer in two seconds
  • The same adjuster then asks a follow-up question

Part What to know
model The model ID (a pinned snapshot on current models)
max_tokens Required; a cap on the output length. If reached, the reply is cut off and stop_reason is max_tokens
system A separate parameter for instructions and context; it is not a message role
messages A list of user and assistant turns; content can be text or blocks (text, image, document, tool_use, tool_result)
Response content A list of blocks: text, tool_use, thinking and others
stop_reason end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn, refusal
usage input_tokens, output_tokens, and the cache fields (Module 3); use it for cost tracking 
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    system="You summarize insurance claim files. Cite the source page.",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": claim_text + "\n\nSummarize and list missing documents."}],
)
print(response.content[0].text, response.usage.output_tokens)

Stateless, so you resend the conversation

  • The API remembers nothing between requests. For a follow-up question, send the whole conversation so far (earlier user and assistant turns) plus the new question.
  • The context window is everything the model can see in one request, including its own reply. It grows with every turn, so long conversations need management (Module 9).
  • Log the request-id response header of every call: it is the key for support and for tracing (Module 16).
Exam tip

"The model forgot what the user said earlier" in an API application means the history was not sent again, not that the model is faulty.

Exam tip

The API is stateless: a follow-up that "forgot" earlier turns means the history was not resent.

3Streaming

With stream: true, the response arrives as server-sent events (SSE) so the user sees text while the model is still writing. It improves perceived latency; total time is about the same.

Event Meaning
message_start A message object with empty content
content_block_start / content_block_delta / content_block_stop One content block: text arrives as text_delta, tool input as input_json_delta (partial JSON), thinking as thinking_delta
message_delta Top-level changes: stop_reason and cumulative usage
message_stop The end
ping Keep-alive; ignore
error The API can send an error mid-stream, for example overloaded_error
  • Assemble text by appending deltas. For a tool call, collect the partial JSON and parse it when the block stops, not before.
  • Handle an error event by retrying or reporting, keeping the partial output only if it is useful. A stream that ends without message_stop is incomplete.
  • Use streaming for chat and long outputs; for background jobs a normal call or a batch is simpler.

4Multi-Format Input: Images and PDFs

Input How to provide it Limits and notes
Image Base64 in the request, a URL, or a file_id from the Files API (upload once, reference many times) Up to 8000 by 8000 pixels per image; many images per request (up to 600) but the request size limit (128 MB on the first-party API) can be reached first; large images are resized and cost visual tokens; on Amazon Bedrock and Google-managed Vertex only base64 is available
PDF A document block (base64, URL or file) Each page is converted to an image plus extracted text; up to 600 pages per request (100 when the context window is under 1M); dense PDFs can fill the context first
Text Text blocks Put long documents before the question; wrap them with clear tags

  • Token cost of images and PDFs counts toward the context window and the bill; check with the token counting endpoint before sending large files Beyond the guide.
  • Large or repeated files: use the Files API instead of resending base64 on every turn.
  • Quality tips: place images before the text instruction, make each image legible (resolution), and label multiple images.

[Verify live] Current documentation: 600 images or 600 PDF pages per request, 128 MB request limit, 8000 pixel maximum edge, file_id through the Files API. These limits and the supported formats change; check the vision and PDF pages. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

Large files and many images: check token cost and limits, and use the Files API to upload once and reference many times.

5Exam Q&A

S1A chat application sends only the newest user message each turn, and Claude cannot answer follow-ups that refer to earlier turns. What is the cause and the fix?

  • AThe system parameter is empty; fill it
  • BThe model has no memory; resend the full history with each request
  • CThe temperature is too low; raise it
  • DThe model is too small to keep earlier turns; switch to a larger one
Show the answer

Answer: B. The API is stateless, so every request must carry the earlier turns.

S2Which parameter is required in every Messages API request, besides the model and messages?

  • Astop_sequences
  • Bsystem
  • Ctemperature
  • Dmax_tokens
Show the answer

Answer: D. max_tokens is required in every request because it caps the output length; the others are optional parameters.

S3A response ends mid-sentence with stop_reason: "max_tokens". What happened?

  • AThe output hit the max_tokens limit; raise it or continue the turn
  • BThe model refused the request because the content broke a usage policy
  • CThe model finished normally
  • DThe network dropped
Show the answer

Answer: A. max_tokens means the output limit was reached and the answer is incomplete.

S4Where does the system prompt go in a Messages API request?

  • AIn the separate top-level system parameter
  • BIn a header
  • CAs the first message with role system
  • DInside the last user message only
Show the answer

Answer: A. The system prompt is its own parameter; message roles are user and assistant.

S5An assistant must show text as soon as it is generated. What should the developer enable?

  • AStreaming with stream: true and text_delta events
  • BPrompt caching of the stable instructions, so replies start sooner
  • CA higher max_tokens
  • DBatch processing
Show the answer

Answer: A. Streaming returns server-sent events so text can be shown incrementally.

S6While streaming a tool call, the application tries to parse the tool input after the first input_json_delta and fails. What should it do?

  • AIgnore tool calls in streams until the final message is complete
  • BSwitch the request to batch
  • CParse each fragment as complete JSON as soon as it arrives from the stream
  • DAccumulate the partial JSON fragments and parse after the content block stops
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tool input arrives as partial JSON that is complete only at the end of the block.

S7A request sends a 450-page PDF and fails or is truncated although it is under the page limit. What is a likely cause and remedy?

  • APDFs are not supported
  • BThe system parameter is too long for a request with a PDF attached
  • CDense pages used up the context first; split the document
  • DThe PDF must be converted to text by hand before it can be sent
Show the answer

Answer: C. Each page costs text and image tokens, so dense PDFs can exhaust the context before the page limit.

S8The same 20 MB image is needed in every turn of a long conversation. Which approach reduces overhead?

  • APaste its description into the system prompt only
  • BShrink it to 16 by 16 pixels
  • CUpload it once with the Files API and reference it by file_id
  • DRe-encode it as base64 and send it again in every single request that needs it
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Files API lets you upload once and reference many times.

S9Which TWO statements about the Messages API are correct? Select TWO.

  • AThe conversation history must be sent again with each request
  • BThe system prompt is a message with role system
  • CStreaming makes the total generation time much shorter
  • Dusage reports input and output tokens for cost tracking
  • EThe server stores the conversation between requests
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. The API is stateless and returns usage; streaming improves perceived latency, not total time.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Request model, max_tokens (required), system (separate), messages (user and assistant), optional tools, thinking, output settings
Response content blocks, stop_reason, usage
Stateless Resend the history every request; log request-id
stop_reason end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn, refusal
Streaming SSE: message_start, block start/delta/stop, message_delta (cumulative usage), message_stop, ping, error; assemble deltas; parse tool JSON at block end
Images base64, URL or file_id; ≤ 8000×8000 px; resized; visual tokens; Bedrock base64 only
PDF Page image + text; ≤ 600 pages (100 under a 1M window)
Files API Upload once, reference many times
